title: Allogeneic Bone Marrow Transplantation Fellowship
inst: University of Toronto (Princess Margaret Cancer Centre, UHN)
Department: Department of Medicine, Division of Hematology
Deadline: Applications open 1 July, close 30 November
Eligibility: Completed subspecialty training in internal medicine and/or medical oncology or hematology; eligible for CPSO licensure
International applicants: Non-Canadian applicants who meet CPSO clinical-fellow licensure requirements contact the Fellowship Program Director; citizens of Bahrain, Kuwait, Oman, Qatar, Saudi Arabia and UAE must apply through their sponsoring agency to the PGME Office (UofT PGME page)
Accreditation: University of Toronto Department of Medicine clinical fellowship registered with PGME; does not lead to RCPSC certification (UofT PGME page)
Application method: Contact Claudia Scheckmann, Coordinator, Fellowship & Education (claudia.scheckmann@uhn.ca)
Positions: 2 per year (flexible depending on programme need)
Visa support: PGME Office provides successful sponsored applicants with documentation to apply for a work permit (UofT PGME page); otherwise not stated on official page
Licence requirement: Must be eligible for a CPSO certificate authorizing postgraduate education (educational licence); applicant must be recognized as a specialist in the jurisdiction where they practised (UofT PGME page)
Summary: A two-year clinical fellowship in Ontario's largest allotransplant programme (about 200 related, unrelated and haploidentical transplants a year) at Princess Margaret Cancer Centre.

title: Hematology Clinician-Scientist Fellowship
inst: McGill University
Department: Department of Medicine / PGME, Hematology

Licence requirement: Must be deemed eligible for a training card from the Collège des Médecins du Québec
Summary: A one-year McGill clinical fellowship for haematology clinician-scientists directed by Dr Kelly Davison; candidates must secure funding.
